subject: Velocity.ai performance SLO snapshot & next-step MOP
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@velocity.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@velocity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Velocity.ai performance SLO snapshot & next-step MOP

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and suggested method-of-procedure (MOP) to validate the streaming SLOs we discussed. I summarized the outcomes so we have a single checklist to move into a short pilot.

Key acceptance targets we agreed to validate during pilot (proposed):
- Latency: p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 200ms for streaming token delivery on 256-token responses (client-side measurement).
- Concurrency: baseline 150 concurrent active sessions; graceful degradation to 300 with defined fallback (polling or lower-fidelity model).
- Throughput: sustained 1,800 tokens/sec across the pool (averaged over 60s windows).
- Streaming requirements: chunked SSE with 50ms max inter-chunk gap under normal load; support for late-join resume with KV cache hits >= 90%.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Velocity to share a small sample production trace or representative request distribution (start/end timestamps, avg token length) — we can run a synthetic overlay. Attachment: demo log extract (velocity_demo_logs_10-20.csv).
2) Redwood to provide a short MOP doc with the pilot validation steps and telemetry hooks (we attached a draft: mop_velocity_streaming.pdf).
3) Decide telemetry access: read-only API key for streaming metrics + a short-lived console invite for your infra lead.
4) Timeline: propose a 2-week pilot window beginning as early as next Mon (Oct 26) — includes baseline run, a 75% load run, and a failover test.

Acceptance decision criteria (simple pass/fail):
- Pass if p95 <= 200ms and concurrency baseline 150 sustained for 60m with no more than 3 error spikes >1% in that window.
- Fail if sustained p95 > 250ms or KV cache hit rate < 80% in normal run.

Ben — adding you here for ops/quant recommendations.

Alex/Priya — let me know which artifacts you can share and whether Oct 26 start works for you.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

- velocity_demo_logs_10-20.csv (CSV, 180KB)
- mop_velocity_streaming.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velocity.ai performance SLO snapshot & next-step MOP

Thanks, Mina — this is great and very actionable. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the MOP: 

- The sample trace is attached (stripped of PII) and contains 2,000 requests across our chat UI for the last 48h. The distribution skews short (avg 45 tokens) but we have a tail of longer sessions.
- We do want to test a higher-concurrency scenario (target: 250) to see where the graceful degradation triggers; our goal is to stay within 1.5x baseline without dropping open streams.
- For telemetry access — we can create a read-only service account for the pilot and invite Ben by COB Wed.

One open question on the acceptance criteria: can Redwood report token-level delivery p95 (client-observed) and server-side inference p95 separately? We need both for internal troubleshooting.

We can start Oct 26 for the baseline. Can we lock a 2-hour sync the morning of Oct 26 to run through the MOP with infra? Jordan will join as our infra lead.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product, Velocity.ai
alex@velocity.ai

Attachment: velocity_demo_trace_10-20_redacted.csv (CSV, 250KB)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@velocity.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@velocity.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velocity.ai performance SLO snapshot & next-step MOP

Alex — perfect, thanks for the trace and the concurrency ask. Quick answers inline: 

- We will provide both client-observed token-delivery p95 and server-side inference p95. Server-side p95 excludes network egress and client assembly time; we'll document method in the MOP.
- 250 concurrency test looks reasonable as an extended run (we'll label it "stress validation") — outcome will determine ramp/burst recommendations.
- Read-only service account is ideal; once Ben has access we'll add console event hooks so you can see token-by-token timing.

Proposed sync: Oct 26 at 09:00 PT — Mina, Ben, Stephanie from Redwood; Alex, Jordan, Priya from Velocity. I'll share a short agenda (20m planning, 40m pilot kickoff run, 20m debrief).

Pilot phases (proposed MOP summary):
1) Baseline run (2h): 150 concurrent simulated sessions, synthetic mix from provided trace — capture p50/p95 token-delivery and server p95.
2) Sustained throughput (1h): step up to target throughput to validate 1,800 tokens/sec aggregate.
3) Stress validation (30m): ramp to 250 concurrency and observe graceful fallback; record error modes and recovery.
4) Failover test (15m): simulate regional latency bump and validate model fallback or lower-fidelity variant.

Deliverables after pilot: consolidated dashboard, raw logs extract, and a single-line decision recommendation (go/no-go for production rollout).

Ben/Stephanie — can you review the attached MOP and confirm instrumentation and any additional synthetic scenarios we should include?

Thanks — Mina

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex@velocity.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@velocity.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@velocity.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Velocity.ai performance SLO snapshot & next-step MOP

Looping in brief ops guidance and the final MOP link. I validated the instrumentation checklist and added two optional scenarios: a) long-session streaming (2k token median) and b) heavy KV-miss workload (simulate cache cold start).

Instrumentation checklist (ops highlights):
- Token-level timestamps (ingress, inference start/end, egress) — required.
- Per-session KV cache hit/miss counters — required.
- SSE inter-chunk gap histogram (ms) — required for streaming SLA.
- Error class tagging: 5xx inference, 4xx client, network timeouts — required.

MOP link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bVelocityPilot (Redwood/Mina/Ben/Stephanie have editor; Velocity has view-only).

Suggested pass/fail thresholds (finalized):
- Pass: client-observed p95 <= 200ms, server p95 <= 150ms, KV cache hit >= 90%, error spikes <= 1% over 60m windows.
- Conditional go: if p95 between 200–250ms but all other metrics pass, recommend short-term mitigation (quantized model variant + caching tune) and re-run stress validation.
- Fail: p95 > 250ms or KV hit < 80% during baseline run.

I uploaded a short synthetic workload script and a CSV with the demo trace we used (attached in prior message).

Action items assigned:
- Velocity: create read-only service account + confirm Oct 26 09:00 PT sync (Alex/Jordan).
- Redwood (Mina): finalize MOP and share pilot runbook by Wed EOD (Oct 21) — completed, link above.
- Redwood (Ben): prepare stress validation runner and upload logs to the Drive folder.

I'll join the Oct 26 kickoff for ops observation.
